chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh al-Qumi al-Faqih informed us, saying: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from 'Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

While al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) was sitting on the lap of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he raised his head and said to him, 'O father, what is the reward for those who visit you after your death?' He replied, 'O my son, whoever comes to me as a visitor after my death will have Paradise; and whoever comes to your father as a visitor after his death will have Paradise; and whoever comes to your brother as a visitor after his death will have Paradise; and whoever comes to you as a visitor after your death will have Paradise.'

key_terms.حَجْر: lap (sitting position of a child on an adult's knees)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Imams after their death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the theological foundation for the cult of the Imams by linking the reward of visiting the Prophet directly to visiting his Ahl al-Bayt, thereby elevating their spiritual status to that of the Messenger. It reflects the Shia emphasis on *Ziyarah* as an act of devotion that bridges the gap between the earthly and the divine, reinforcing the concept of *Tawalli* (affiliation) with the Prophet's family as a means of attaining Paradise.
